To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Chlamydia is the most prevalent bacterial sexually transmitted infection in Europe and that it is asymptomatic in most cases, and that it causes severe reproductive tract complications in women and men, including pelvic inflammatory disease, infertility, ectopic pregnancy and chronic pelvic pain.
Chlamydia infections can be diagnosed and treated effectively, and the majority of infections are asymptomatic, so testing and treatment are crucial to reduce transmission and sequelae.

Chlamydia is a common sexually transmitted infection, and that testing and treatment is important to prevent complications and sequelae, and that testing, diagnostics and treatment should be improved.

the development of new diagnostic tests for Chlamydia infections and their evaluation in clinical trials.
improving access to Chlamydia diagnosis and treatment in order to control Chlamydia infections in Europe.
the diagnosis, treatment, prevention and epidemiology of Chlamydyli infections.
